chunks: He said: And Abdullah ibn Salam Abu Huraira narrated to us from Zur'a from Mufaddal who said:

I was sitting in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when Abu al-Hasan and Muhammad came to him, and with them was a young goat which they were pulling back and forth. Muhammad managed to pull it away from his brother, so Abu al-Hasan felt shy and came and sat beside me. I embraced him and kissed him. Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, he is your master. Despite this, the Banu al-Abbas will seize him and he will endure hardship from them, but Allah will release him from their hands in some manner. Then his affair will be hidden from the people until the eyes shed tears for him and the hearts are agitated for him, just as a ship is agitated in the deep sea amidst wind storms. Then Allah will bring deliverance for this Ummah in religion and the world through his hands.

key_terms.بَنِي الْعَبَّاسِ: The Banu Abbas (the ruling Abbasid dynasty)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the future status and occultation of Musa ibn Ja'far?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* serves as a crucial proof for the Imamate of Musa al-Kadhim (a.s) by highlighting his childhood status as 'Sahib al-Amr' (the Master of Command) while still in his father's care. It specifically addresses the Waqifiya controversy by predicting the Imam's prolonged concealment ('istirar') and the resulting confusion among the masses, culminating in his reappearance to establish justice. The narrative underscores the divine protection of the Imam from Abbasid persecution, framing his occultation as a necessary phase for the ultimate deliverance of the Ummah.
